findings.issue_text: [BUG] `sentry-repo` gitlink/submodule entry added with no `.gitmodules` change, making it a broken gitlink that causes clone/checkout failures in CI and fresh checkouts

[BUG] `error_upsampling.py:33` cache key uses Python's randomized builtin `hash()`, so keys differ across processes, making the 60-second cache permanently miss and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` a silent no-op; key should use stable serialization like `","".join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))`

[BUG] `test_error_upsampling.py:31-35` constructs `SnubaParams(start=None, end=None)` but `start`/`end` are required positional datetime fields, raising TypeError in setUp so the entire test suite errors out before any test runs

[BUG] `error_upsampling.py:97` assumes `sample_weight` is populated for allowlisted projects but nothing in the diff writes it (only `sample_rate` is set in factories.py), so stats report count == 0 or resolver errors; the feature's prerequisite ingestion does not exist

[ADVISORY] Option toggling doesn't trigger `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (no signal hook wired), so operators flipping the allowlist see stale behavior up to 60s or longer across workers; `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller in the diff, making it inert

[ADVISORY] `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` detects error queries only via the literal substring `event.type:error`, so semantically equivalent filters (e.g. `error.type:*`, `is:unresolved`) bypass upsampling, producing silently inconsistent dashboards

[ADVISORY] Unrelated change to error message string in `organization_events_stats.py:121-124` may break tests asserting the old text and should be in its own commit so reverting the feature doesn't revert the fix

[BUG] The 60-second eligibility cache in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is never reset between tests, so partial-allowlist and no-allowlist tests read a stale cached True, causing nondeterministic failures or passing for the wrong reason — the partial-allowlist rejection path through the endpoint is untested

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches the exact literal `count()`, silently skipping aliased counts (`count() as total`), `count(unique(...))`, and any equation containing count, producing mixed-scale output in a single response

[BUG] In the top-events branch, only y_axes/timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns and run_top_events_timeseries_query's top-event selection still use raw `count()`, so top-events tables and timeseries report mutually contradicting counts

[BUG] `upsampled_count` declares default_result_type="number" while every other count-style function uses "integer", so upsampled counts are formatted as floats/decimal-precision values in widget rendering

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller in the diff (dead code), so the documented invalidation story for the 60s cache does not exist; even if called it only deletes the exact `{org}:{hash(sorted(project_ids))}` key, not keys for differing project sets, making invalidation combinatorially incomplete

[ADVISORY] No production writer for `sample_weight` exists in the diff; the SnQL function sums Column("sample_weight") but nothing in application code computes or writes that column during ingestion, so error counts could silently become 0 when the option is enabled — the end-to-end sample_weight population criterion is unverified

[ADVISORY] The public entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects has zero direct tests; the cache-hit path short-circuit semantics and cache-key construction (hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))) are untested behaviors

[ADVISORY] `hash()` is used to build a cache key shared across processes; for non-int elements or string-typed project IDs, PYTHONHASHSEED randomization makes the key differ per process, collapsing cache hit rates and breaking invalidation
[ADVISORY] Unrelated sentry-repo git submodule added with zero references in code, CI, or tests — scope drift causing every clone/CI run to pull an unrelated nested repository with no justification

[ADVISORY] 400 response text silently changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1' — unrelated copy fix invisible in the feature PR, breaking clients/tests asserting the old message

[ADVISORY] Read path assumes sample_weight column exists and is populated for allowlisted projects, but no ingestion/writer for sample_weight exists in the diff (no event normalizer, snuba schema change, or migration), so sum(sample_weight) returns 0/NULL and dashboards silently report zero error counts

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wired unconditionally into store_event for all test events with an error_sampling context, not gated on allowlist/project/feature tests — silently overwrites sample_rate in unrelated tests

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is exported public helper but has no call site, so the documented contract of invalidating cache on allowlist changes is unenforced — operators wait up to 60s with stale eligibility and the function is dead code

[BUG] Stray `sentry-repo` submodule/gitlink at repo root pointing to commit `a5d290951d...` — an accidentally-committed nested repo clone causing dangling subproject entries, failing `git submodule update` and breaking reproducible builds

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` uses raw substring match `"event.type:error" in query`, so negated filters like `query=!event.type:error` or `query=-event.type:error` also match, wrongly swapping `count()` for `sum(sample_weight)` on transaction queries where `sample_weight` doesn't exist

[BUG] `upsampled_count` aggregate `sum(sample_weight)` has no COALESCE/default; events with NULL `sample_weight` (pre-allowlist or bypassing ingestion paths) are skipped by Snuba's sum, silently showing 0 or drastically understated counts

[BUG] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only transforms the exact string `count()`; `count_unique(user)`, `failure_count()`, and aliased forms like `count() as total` pass through, producing mixed upsampled/raw denominators in the same response and wrong derived ratios/equations

[BUG] Eligibility cache key is only `org + project_ids` with no invalidation — `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has zero call sites, so allowlist changes via `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist")` only take effect after TTL expiry, contradicting the documented invalidation contract

[ADVISORY] Unconditional `cache.get`/`cache.set` added per stats request to avoid an `options.get` that is already an in-process in-memory lookup — adds a Redis/memcache roundtrip per request and increases shared cache load, opposite of the optimization's intent

[ADVISORY] Transform is wired into only organization-events-stats endpoint while issues list, event details, dashboards, and issues stream endpoints serve the same `count()` semantics untransformed, giving users inconsistent upsampled vs raw counts across the UI

[ADVISORY] All-projects-or-nothing gating: partial allowlists cause `all()` to return False and silently fall back to raw `count()`, undercounting allowlisted projects while counting non-allowlisted ones normally — a mixed-denominator total with no signal to the user

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses bare `except Exception: pass` blocks around `.get()` chains in the shared `store_event` factory, silently injecting `sample_rate` into unrelated test fixtures and hiding real shape errors (e.g. non-mapping `contexts`), making future upsampling test failures hard to diagnose

[BUG] `error_upsampling.py:35-48`: The 60-second eligibility cache silently redefines semantics from "all projects are allowlisted now" to "allowlisted as of up to 60 seconds ago" — a behavioral change not accepted by human decision; removing a project from the allowlist still returns inflated/incorrect counts for up to 60 seconds
[BUG] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line ~76) has zero callers anywhere in the diff — no hook on options changes, so the invalidation path the cache design depends on is dead code

[BUG] `error_upsampling.py:130-138`: `_is_error_focused_query` uses raw substring check `"event.type:error" in query`, so mixed or negated discover queries get full upsampling applied to rows with no `sample_weight`, producing wrong counts (e.g., `event.type:error event.type:transaction` or `!event.type:error`)
[ADVISORY] A `sentry-repo` git submodule pointing at commit `a5d290951d...` was accidentally committed at the repository root, unrelated to the change; it should be removed before merge

[ADVISORY] `test_organization_events_stats.py:3565+`: endpoint tests exercise the real shared cache, so eligibility results persist across tests in the same class — order-dependent flakiness masking real behavior if test ordering or project-id combinations change

[ADVISORY] The cache-hit branch of `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled` (the code path introduced by the performance optimization) is never covered by any test with a previously-cached stale value — no regression guard for the new behavior

[ADVISORY] `error_upsampling.py:103-107` and `discover.py:1041-1052`: the core assumption that sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects is asserted only in comments with no validation, feature flag, or rollback mechanism; if sample_weight is missing, all count() figures silently become wrong with no circuit breaker

[ADVISORY] `organization_events_stats.py:218-306`: upsampling transformation is applied only to y_axes/timeseries_columns; the top-events path leaves selected_columns (typically including count()) untransformed, so a single topEvents response carries upsampled series data alongside unupsampled per-event totals, showing contradictory count values

[BUG] In `_is_error_focused_query` (error_upsampling.py:137-141), the error-query gate is a raw substring test (`if "event.type:error" in query: return True`) that cannot distinguish an affirmative filter from a negated one (e.g. `!event.type:error`), causing `count()` to be silently rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` for result sets containing non-upsampled/transaction events, returning wildly wrong event counts (up to 10x multiplier per the 0.1 sample rate); the substring also falsely fires when the literal appears inside a free-text search term such as `message:"event.type:error"`.

[BUG] In error_upsampling.py:19-21, the cache short-circuit caches only the project-allowlist half under a key with no namespace isolation beyond org id, with no version/invalidation tie-in to the global option; when an operator removes a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, requests still sum `sample_weight` and return inflated counts for up to 60 seconds because `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has zero call sites (no caller, no options-change hook), making the documented invalidation path dead code and the 'eventual consistency is acceptable' doc comment an unmet operational guarantee.

[ADVISORY] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` (error_upsampling.py:103-113) relies on an unchecked schema assumption that `sample_weight` exists for all events in allowlisted projects; events written before client sampling was enabled or by old SDKs have no `sample_weight`, so `sum(sample_weight)` silently counts them as 0 (or errors), understating error counts on dashboards used to page on error spikes and producing retroactively wrong historical charts for existing projects with a `statsPeriod` predating SDK rollout.

[ADVISORY] The public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is never invoked by any test in the diff, so the caching logic (cache-hit short-circuit, `cache.set(..., 60)` TTL, and the cached-result re-check) has zero direct coverage; a regression in the cache-key construction (e.g. `hash(tuple(sorted(...)))`, which is not stable across processes under `PYTHONHASHSEED`) would not fail any test
[ADVISORY] Endpoint tests only ever hit the cache-miss path because they use fresh org/project IDs per test, so the cache-hit branch is effectively dead code in the test suite

[ADVISORY] The assertion `data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10` depends on unverifiable infrastructure: the population of `sample_weight` in Snuba lives in the pinned submodule, and if the submodule doesn't map `sample_rate`→`sample_weight` the test fails or the diff's headline behavior is unverified

[ADVISORY] Inline comment says "First bucket has 1 event" while asserting 10 — the comment contradicts the assertion, and no test asserts a second, different sample rate (e.g. 0.5 → ×2) to prove the value isn't coincidental

[ADVISORY] The upsampling transformation is wired into four distinct query paths but every endpoint test only hits the plain non-top-events timeseries path; the `top_events > 0 and upsampling_enabled` branch has no test triggering it, so a regression there (e.g. dropping `final_columns` back to `query_columns` or a `count` alias collision) passes the entire suite

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is exported public API with no caller and no test; its key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, so invalidation requires passing the exact same project-id set as the query that populated the cache — a project-list query with different membership never invalidates, making staleness unbounded for multi-project dashboards

[ADVISORY] `_is_error_focused_query` requires the literal substring `event.type:error` in the raw query string, so a discover query with no `event.type` filter (which returns both errors and transactions) is treated as non-error and silently skips upsampling, undercounting errors; this unfiltered case is untested with zero assertions pinning it down

[BUG] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction sums a `sample_weight` column that no migration or backfill in this diff guarantees exists or is populated in the errors dataset, so queries against pre-existing events execute `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` over NULL rows, silently showing 0 instead of real counts.

[BUG] The only write path for the sampling context is the test factory; no production event-ingestion code populates `sample_weight`, leaving a reader with no writer — the real ingestion change may live in the sentry-repo gitlink (a5d290951de) whose contents are not reviewable, so migration safety cannot be established from this diff.

[BUG] The cache key in `invalidate_upsampling_cache`/eligibility check uses Python's `hash(tuple(...))`, which is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so cache invalidation fails across pods and queries keep returning upsampled counts for removed projects; a stable hash (e.g. sorted comma-joined ids) should be used.

[ADVISORY] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` only on exact whole-column-string match, so equation fields and `count_unique(...)` pass through untransformed, mixing upsampled and raw series in one widget with numbers differing by the inverse sample rate.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` matches the raw substring "event.type:error" anywhere in the lowercased query string, so a negated discover query like `!event.type:error` (or `NOT event.type:error`, or a parenthesized exclusion) passes the check and gets its `count()` rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`, which is null/absent on transaction and non-sampled events, silently returning 0 or null-coerced counts with a 200 OK

[BUG] The transform is applied whenever `dataset == errors`, but the rewritten y-axis `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is only registered in discover's `function_converter`, so errors-dataset requests with allowlisted projects reach the resolver with an unknown function name, causing a 500 or wrong-shaped 400 on the primary code path of this feature

[BUG] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites only the literal `count()`, so a request with `yAxis=count(),count_unique(user)` produces one upsampled axis and one raw axis in the same response, returning 200 with internally inconsistent data (counts scaled by sample_weight, unique-user counts un-scaled) with no indication which is which

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has zero call sites in the diff and only deletes the exact key for the passed project-ID tuple, so invalidating project X leaves every cached key containing X alongside other projects stale; the invalidation function is dead code operators cannot actually invoke

[ADVISORY] `upsampled_count`'s snql aggregate is `sum(sample_weight)` with no null handling or defaulting, but error events ingested before the allowlist sampling shipped have no `sample_weight` value, so once a project is allowlisted all its historical errors sum to null/0 — a silent data regression where event-count charts drop historical counts to zero

[ADVISORY] The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, so if `project_ids` is None, `sorted(None)` raises TypeError inside `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, which is called unconditionally for every stats request, turning a previously valid request into an unhandled 500

[ADVISORY] The three branches in organization_events_stats.py each recompute `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` with identical copy-pasted calls, and the top-events RPC branch does not apply the transform to `get_field_list` (raw_groupby/selected_columns), so a top-events request selecting `count()` gets upsampled y-axes but raw selected-column counts in the same response; extraction to a single transform point would delete the three duplicated blocks

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps the context read in a bare `except Exception: pass` twice, silently swallowing malformed contexts in test factory code, meaning a test with a typo'd `error_sampling` context proceeds with no `sample_rate` set and asserts against un-upsampled data, passing for the wrong reason

[ADVISORY] The eligibility cache stores the allowlist verdict keyed by `(org, project_ids)` for 60s, but the docstring in `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims config "reads fresh each time", which the cache directly contradicts; requests flip between upsampled and raw counts within the cache window, producing non-deterministic chart values that are hard to diagnose because the comment points at the wrong mechanism

However, the finding’s claim that endpoint tests will read a stale cached `True` across tests is not verifiable from the diff: each test method’s `setUp` creates new projects (and likely a new org via `create_project()`/base `setUp`), which would change `organization.id` and project IDs, producing a different cache key per test. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches the exact literal `count()`, silently skipping aliased counts (`count() as total`), `count(unique(...))`, and any equation containing count, producing mixed-scale output in a single response

adjudication.rationale: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only transforms when `column.lower().strip() == "count()"` and otherwise leaves the column untouched. That means strings like `"count() as total"`, other `count(...)` variants, or equations containing `count()` will not be upsampled, while a plain `count()` in the same `query_columns` list *will* be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count`. Since `organization_events_stats.py` applies this transformation to `y_axes`/`selected_columns` as-is, a request with multiple yAxes can produce inconsistently-scaled results within the same response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the top-events branch, only y_axes/timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns and run_top_events_timeseries_query's top-event selection still use raw `count()`, so top-events tables and timeseries report mutually contradicting counts

adjudication.rationale: In the top-events branch (`if top_events > 0`), the diff shows `query_columns` being conditionally transformed into `final_columns` and then consistently passed as `y_axes` (RPC) or `timeseries_columns` (non-RPC). The `selected_columns` argument is not derived from `query_columns` at all; it is `self.get_field_list(...)` (groupby/display fields), so the claim that `selected_columns` still uses raw `count()` is not supported by the diff. Also, the diff does not show any separate “top-event selection” query that uses raw `count()`; only `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` is passed through, but whether that contains `count()` and affects top-event ranking is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `upsampled_count` declares default_result_type="number" while every other count-style function uses "integer", so upsampled counts are formatted as floats/decimal-precision values in widget rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `upsampled_count` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py` with `default_result_type="number"` while the SnQL it generates is explicitly `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, i.e., an integer-valued expression. That mismatch could affect downstream type-driven formatting/serialization, but the diff alone doesn’t prove widget rendering will show floats/decimals or that all other count-like functions use `"integer"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller in the diff (dead code), so the documented invalidation story for the 60s cache does not exist; even if called it only deletes the exact `{org}:{hash(sorted(project_ids))}` key, not keys for differing project sets, making invalidation combinatorially incomplete

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, but there is no call site shown anywhere in this PR, so the documented “should be called when the allowlist configuration changes” invalidation mechanism is not actually wired up (dead/unused API in this diff). Also, the cache key is specific to an exact `organization_id` + `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`; the invalidator deletes only that exact key, so it cannot invalidate cached eligibility results for other project-id combinations that may have been cached for the same org (combinatorially incomplete), as the finding states.
